classification.difficultyReason: Construct the sloped pool model, find its total capacity, then recognise the evaporated layer as a rectangular volume while water still covers the base.

content.prompt: A pool is 50 metres long, 25 metres wide, 1 m deep at one end and 2 m deep at the other.

children.label: a
children.prompt: Draw a diagram of the pool. What 3D solid is this?

answer.worked: Trapezoidal prism: the vertical cross-section along the length is a trapezium, repeated across the width.

spec.description: Labelled pool sketch with rectangular horizontal top and straight sloping floor; vertical end depths differ.
spec.mathematics: Model top vertices A=(0,0,0), B=(50,0,0), C=(50,25,0), D=(0,25,0). Floor vertices E=(0,0,-1), F=(50,0,-2), G=(50,25,-2), H=(0,25,-1). Faces ABCD, ABFE, BCGF, CDHG, DAEH, EFGH. View towards the viewer (+,-,+): top boundary, front and right faces visible; EH, HG and DH concealed. Depth is visually exaggerated for legibility; all dimensions retain the givens. Straight floor follows the supplied trapezoidal-prism answer.
spec.answerVisibility: Answer-only drawing; labels 50 m, 25 m, 1 m and 2 m.

children.label: b
children.prompt: Calculate the capacity of the pool in kilolitres.

answer.worked:
$$\begin{align*}A &= \frac{50}{2}(1+2)\\A &= 75\text{ m}^2\\V &= Ah\\V &= 75\times25\\V &= 1875\text{ m}^3\end{align*}$$
Since $1\text{ m}^3=1\text{ kL}$, the capacity is $1875\text{ kL}$.

children.label: c
children.prompt: If the level of the pool dropped by 75 cm on a hot day, calculate how much water is needed to replace the evaporated water, answer in kilolitres.

answer.worked:
$75\text{ cm}=0.75\text{ m}$. The water still covers the whole base because $0.75<1$.
$$\begin{align*}A &= 25\times50\\A &= 1250\text{ m}^2\\V &= Ah\\V &= 1250\times0.75\\V &= 937.5\text{ m}^3\end{align*}$$
The replacement water is $937.5\text{ kL}$.
